title: Finite monogenic cover with normal principal open
statement: Let R be a normal Nagata domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], K its fraction field, x in K, S=R[x], m a maximal ideal of S, and A=S_m [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. There exists a Noetherian domain B [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with an injective finite A-algebra map [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and a nonzero f such that every prime localization of B_f [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is a normal domain. For every maximal ideal q of B there exist a normal Noetherian Nagata domain Rprime, its fraction field Kprime, y in Kprime, a Noetherian monogenic algebra Rprime[y], and a maximal ideal n containing y, together with a ring isomorphism B_q ≅ Rprime[y]_n. The quantified rings lie in Type(max u v). This construction does not assume or conclude analytic unramifiedness.

proof.text: R is Noetherian by the Nagata definition, and S=R[x] is a finite type algebra, hence Noetherian. Therefore A=S_m is Noetherian. Since B is finite over A, B is Noetherian. Rprime is Noetherian by its Nagata property, and each one-generator algebra Rprime[y] is Noetherian by the finite type theorem.

proof.text: For a maximal q of B, contract to n0 in T=Rprime[z] and take r in Rprime with z-r in n0. Set y=z-r. The two monogenic subalgebras are equal: y belongs to Rprime[z] by subtraction, and z=y+r belongs to Rprime[y] by addition. The induced ring equivalence transports n0 to a maximal n containing y. Mathlib iterated localization identifies B_q with T_n0; compose this with the localized ring equivalence T_n0 to Rprime[y]_n.

proof.text: Write z=b/a in the fraction field of Rprime with a nonzero. Realize Rprime_a as a subalgebra of Kprime; it contains z, and is an away localization of T=Rprime[z] at the image aT of a. Its normality transports to T_aT. Let f be the image of aT in B=Localization M, nonzero by injectivity. A prime localization of B_f is, by iterated localization, the localization T_p at its contraction p. The image aT is outside p because f is a unit in B_f. Hence T_p is a localization of the normal domain T_aT and is a normal domain. This constructs the required principal open and proves normality at all its primes.

theorem exists_finite_cover_adjoin_singleton_core
    (R : Type u) (K : Type v) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsIntegrallyClosed R]
    [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K] (hR : IsNagataRing R) (x : K)
    (m : Ideal (Algebra.adjoin R ({x} : Set K))) [m.IsMaximal] :
    ∃ (B : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : IsDomain B)
      (_ : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime m) B) (_ : IsNoetherianRing B),
      Function.Injective (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime m) B) ∧
      Module.Finite (Localization.AtPrime m) B ∧
      (∃ f : B, f ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ (p : Ideal (Localization.Away f)) [p.IsPrime],
        IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Localization.AtPrime p)) ∧
      (∀ (q : Ideal B) [q.IsMaximal],
        ∃ (R' K' : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : IsDomain R')
          (_ : IsIntegrallyClosed R') (_ : IsNoetherianRing R') (_ : Field K')
          (_ : Algebra R' K') (_ : IsFractionRing R' K'),
          IsNagataRing R' ∧ ∃ (y : K')
            (_ : IsNoetherianRing (Algebra.adjoin R' ({y} : Set K')))
            (n : Ideal (Algebra.adjoin R' ({y} : Set K'))) (_ : n.IsMaximal),
            (⟨y, Algebra.subset_adjoin (Set.mem_singleton y)⟩ :
              Algebra.adjoin R' ({y} : Set K')) ∈ n ∧
              Nonempty (Localization.AtPrime q ≃+* Localization.AtPrime n))
